FALSE POSITIVE: dependency-check matches the LINE Messaging API SDK against CVEs filed against the LINE *consumer messenger* client for iOS/Android (cpe:/a:line:line). The vulnerable CPE is for an unrelated product family — a server-side bot SDK cannot reach an iOS TLS-verification or Android integer-overflow bug. Confirmed against security-report-2026-06-15.md.
(The original 0.9.2 note said "WhatsApp mobile client" here; that was a copy-paste slip from the camel-whatsapp entry below — the product is LINE. Corrected 2026-09-08.)
2026-09-08: widened from line-bot-jackson to every com.linecorp.bot:line-bot-* artifact. The scan showed the same inherited records (CVE-2023-5554 at 9.8, CVE-2019-6010, CVE-2021-41011, CVE-2022-41568, the CVE-2025-1402x family) on line-bot-webhook and line-bot-client-base as well.

FALSE POSITIVE: Apache Camel's Telegram component (camel-telegram) is consistently misidentified as the Telegram Messenger client. The NVD CPE record for "telegram_messenger" matches every artifact whose name starts with "telegram"; CVE records like CVE-2024-* on the Messenger app are not reachable via a Camel webhook receiver. Confirmed against security-report-2026-06-15.md.
2026-09-08: this long-form CPE turned out to match nothing in practice — dependency-check actually assigns the SHORT form cpe:2.3:a:telegram:telegram to these artifacts (confirmed by reading `vulnerabilityIds` out of the JSON report). The entry is retained because the long form is what NVD registers for some Telegram records; the short-form entry in the Class 1 block below is the one that does the work. The camel CPE (cpe:2.3:a:apache:camel) is deliberately NOT suppressed on any entry — a real Apache Camel CVE must still fail the build.

FALSE POSITIVE: Telegram *client* CVEs matched against artifacts whose name merely contains "telegram" — Apache Camel's Telegram component and JaiClaw's own Telegram adapters. CVE-2019-10044 (8.8), CVE-2024-7014 (8.1) and CVE-2021-31320/31321 (7.1) are all against the Telegram desktop/mobile applications. These four are pinned by CVE id as a belt-and-braces layer; the short-form cpe:2.3:a:telegram:telegram entry below is what covers the whole family (13+ records) without enumerating ids.

FALSE POSITIVE: io.jaiclaw:jaiclaw-channel-whatsapp is JaiClaw's own WhatsApp *channel adapter*. dependency-check derives a CPE from the artifact name and matches cpe:/a:whatsapp:whatsapp, inheriting the entire WhatsApp mobile-client CVE history — 15 records at CVSS 9.8 (CVE-2018-6349/6350, CVE-2019-3568, CVE-2019-11933, CVE-2020-1891/ 1907/1909, CVE-2021-24026/24041/24042, CVE-2022-36934 and others). These are buffer overflows and RCEs in the Android/iOS WhatsApp application. This artifact is a Spring adapter that speaks the WhatsApp Business HTTP API; none of that native client code exists here. Confirmed by the 2026-09-08 NVD-backed scan.

FALSE POSITIVE: Apache Camel's WhatsApp *starter* — the Spring Boot packaging of camel-whatsapp, matched against the WhatsApp mobile client CPE for the same reason as the camel-whatsapp entry above. The starter is a thin auto-configuration wrapper; the WhatsApp native-client CVEs (CVE-2020-1907 et al.) are unreachable.

Both are Android Activity components; this is a server-side Java module with no Android code. Confirmed by the 2026-09-08 NVD-backed scan.
See the jaiclaw-tasks / Tasks.org entry above.

FALSE POSITIVE: spring-cloud-starter-vault-config is assigned cpe:2.3:a:vmware:spring_cloud_config (confidence HIGHEST) purely on the "config" name fragment. The three flagged records — CVE-2026-40982 (9.1 CRITICAL, directory traversal in spring-cloud-config-server), CVE-2026-41002 (8.1, TOCTOU on spring.cloud.config.server.git.basedir) and CVE-2026-40981 (7.5, GCP Secrets Manager backend cross-project exposure) — are all against Spring Cloud *Config Server*, a different artifact. Verified 2026-09-08: spring-cloud-config-server and spring-cloud-starter-config appear nowhere in the reactor; JaiClaw uses Spring Cloud *Vault* to mount HashiCorp Vault secrets as property sources. The vulnerable server code is not on the classpath.

FALSE POSITIVE: com.paypal.sdk:paypal-server-sdk (a server-side REST SDK) matches the PayPal *Android application* CPE. Both flagged records are from 2013 and explicitly scoped to the mobile app: CVE-2013-7202 (8.1) "The WebHybridClient class in PayPal 5.3 and earlier for Android" and CVE-2013-7201 (7.4) "WebHybridClient.java ... ignores SSL errors". There is no WebHybridClient in a server SDK. Confirmed by the 2026-09-08 scan.
FALSE POSITIVE: see the CVE-2013-7201 entry above — same artifact, same PayPal-for-Android mismatch.

FALSE POSITIVE (wrong language binding): CVE-2026-0994 (7.5) is a recursion-depth DoS in google.protobuf.json_format.ParseDict() — the *Python* protobuf runtime. The flagged artifact is protobuf-java. The vulnerable ParseDict entry point does not exist in the Java runtime. Confirmed by the 2026-09-08 scan (5 modules, all via transitive google-cloud / gRPC dependencies).

FALSE POSITIVE (wrong artifact): CVE-2026-42582 (7.5) is in io.netty.handler.codec.http3.QpackDecoder#decodeHuffmanEncodedLiteral, fixed in 4.2.13.Final. dependency-check flags netty-transport 4.1.135.Final because the CPE matches the netty *product* at that version, but the QPACK/HTTP3 decoder does not live in netty-transport. Verified 2026-09-08 on the jaiclaw-gateway tree: the artifact that actually contains the vulnerable class, io.netty:netty-codec-http3, resolves to 4.2.15.Final — already past the 4.2.13 fix. This closes the "re-evaluate the netty pin in the next CVE scan" TODO in the root POM's CVE-override block.
Scoped to the io.netty group at the 4.1.x line rather than to individual artifacts: the assigned CPE is cpe:2.3:a:netty:netty, which matches the netty *product* at 4.1.135, so EVERY 4.1.x artifact on the classpath inherits this record — netty-codec, netty-transport, netty-transport-classes-epoll, netty-transport-native-unix-common, netty-handler, and so on. Chasing them by artifact name would be an open-ended list. The HTTP/3 codec that actually contains the vulnerable class is versioned independently (4.2.15.Final) and is NOT covered by this suppression — if netty-codec-http3 is ever flagged below 4.2.13, that is a real finding and must be fixed, not suppressed.

FALSE POSITIVE: io.jaiclaw:jaiclaw-ascii-render is JaiClaw's own ASCII box/diagram renderer. dependency-check matches it against the Element Matrix client CPE (cpe:/a:element:element_*) on the word "element", inheriting CVE-2022-41904 (6.5, Element iOS Megolm trust), CVE-2025-27606 (4.6, Element Android PIN logout) and CVE-2024-26132 (3.3, Element Android file sharing). All three are against the Element Matrix mobile clients; this artifact renders text boxes and has no Matrix, crypto, or Android code. Confirmed by the 2026-09-08 NVD-backed scan (flagged in 4 modules).
FALSE POSITIVE: companion to the jaiclaw-ascii-render entry above — the Element Android/iOS CPEs are registered under several product names, so match by CVE as well to cover the variants.
See the jaiclaw-ascii-render / Element entries above.
See the jaiclaw-ascii-render / Element entries above.

NOT REACHABLE: CVE-2025-67030 (8.8) is a directory traversal in org.codehaus.plexus.util.Expand#extractFile — archive extraction. plexus-utils 3.5.1 reaches JaiClaw only as a *provided*-scope transitive of maven-plugin-api 3.9.8 in jaiclaw-maven-plugin, i.e. it is supplied by the Maven runtime at build time and is never packaged into or shipped with any JaiClaw artifact. Verified 2026-09-08: none of the five Mojos (Analyze, Scaffold, VerifyDeploy, ComplianceReport, Catalog) reference plexus Expand or perform archive extraction. Re-evaluate if the plugin ever gains an unpack step; the fix is plexus-utils >= 4.0.1.

FALSE POSITIVE (wrong artifact + already-patched version): CVE-2026-23907 (5.3) and CVE-2026-33929 (4.3) are path-traversal flaws in the *ExtractEmbeddedFiles example*, which ships in pdfbox-examples — not in the core pdfbox artifact. The advisory ranges also end at 3.0.6 ("from 3.0.0 through 3.0.6"), so the pinned 3.0.7 is already past the fix; dependency-check matches on the pdfbox product CPE regardless of sub-artifact. Verified 2026-09-08: pdfbox-examples and ExtractEmbeddedFiles appear nowhere in the reactor. Same reasoning covers the xmpbox 2.0.24 companion flagged in jaiclaw-html-pdf.
FALSE POSITIVE: see the CVE-2026-23907 entry above — same pdfbox-examples / ExtractEmbeddedFiles mismatch.

VENDOR-DISPUTED, and not reachable with attacker-controlled input. CVE-2023-51079 (5.3) reports that MVEL ParseTools.subCompileExpression can take a long time to compile expressions with many Java class lookups. The NVD record carries an explicit vendor dispute: "the only thing that you could expect is that the parser will take a crazy amount of time to complete its task." mvel2 reaches JaiClaw only as a transitive of drools-mvel in the optional jaiclaw-rules module, where DRL rules are authored by the deploying operator, not supplied by end users. Re-evaluate if jaiclaw-rules ever compiles user-submitted DRL.

FALSE POSITIVE (telegram name collision). Telegram desktop/mobile client CVEs matched against server-side Bot API adapters (Apache Camel components + JaiClaw channel/docstore adapters). dependency-check derives a CPE from the artifact name, so these server-side Java artifacts inherit the consumer application's CVE history. Suppressed by CVE id: <cpe> suppression was verified NOT to work for these records on dependency-check 12.1.0 (tested with the short product form, the full versioned form, and a regex form — all three still failed the build), whereas <cve> suppression works. Full CVE set taken from the 2026-09-08 full-reactor scan.
